chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darradj, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who visits the House (Kaaba) before shaving [his head], and he said, 'It is not proper except that he be forgetful.'

Then he said, 'Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was visited by some people on the Day of Sacrifice. Some of them said, 'O Messenger of Allah, I shaved before I sacrificed,' and some said, 'I shaved before I threw [the pebbles].' They did not leave anything that they ought to have delayed except that they hastened it. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'There is no blame [on them].'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim shaves his head before throwing the pebbles at the Jamarat?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that the sequence of Hajj rituals (halq, dhabh, rami) is recommended (mustahabb) rather than strictly obligatory (wajib), as evidenced by the Prophet’s declaration of 'no blame' (la haraj) when companions performed them out of order. It highlights the Shia scholarly principle of leniency in ritual sequencing, noting that only forgetfulness or haste exempts the pilgrim from penalty, thereby preserving the validity of Hajj even if the canonical order is reversed.
